items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: Teddy and Roy, I played with them in 1930 -- '29 and '30.

ctx.x: Right. Or were there a lot of good musicians then, too?

Well, there were quite a few good musicians around. Teddy and Roy, I played with them in 1930 -- '29 and '30. So I know they were good! We had a good band. But the guys around them days were able to sit in, oh, up to around '35 or '36, '37 maybe...maybe clear up to '40... Then the War started, and a number of guys left and (?). I guess a lot of them learned a lot by going into the Army and getting...

items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: and had Vic Dickinson on trombone and Bob Wilber on reeds

ctx.x: That's right. He's very happy these days.

Yeah, I work quite often with him at jazz festivals. Of course, recently up there in Colorado Springs, Gibson's party. And I did a record date I'm proud of called "Teddy Wilson's All Starts" for the Chiaroscuro label a couple years ago when he was on trumpet, and had Vic Dickinson on trombone and Bob Wilber on reeds. Bob, incidentally, did the little sketch arrangements this time. And Major Haley on bass and we had Oliver Jackson on drums. And we tried to do kind of like we did in the old days. We made three…
